issues.subcategory: Child warning studies may not be memory conformity studies
issues.description: Child warning studies may not be memory conformity studies: The child-study sentence may blur strict memory-conformity evidence with broader warning/suggestibility evidence: Price & Connolly is described as a biasing-interview paradigm, not as co-witness misinformation under the paper’s definition. This makes it unclear whether those child studies are intended as memory-conformity interventions or adjacent warning evidence.
issues.quote: However, in other studies (Bodner et al., 2009 ; Meade \& Roediger, 2002), it was demonstrated that warning can significantly decrease, but not completely eliminate, the number of mistakes. Similarly, Cadavid and Luna (2021) found that an extensive warning reduced the memory conformity effect. There are also two studies of this kind involving children; in the first (Price \& Connolly, 2004), children were engaged in play sessions and afterwards they were given a biasing interview. 'Logic of opposition' instructions, i.e., informing the children that "the reviewer from yesterday accidentally said some things that were wrong", were applied. A warning of this kind did not prevent the children from reporting the misinformation. In another study (Principe, Haines, Adkins, \& Guiliano, 2010), a warning against co-witness misinformation reduced suggestibility in children, at least in some experimental conditions.

issues.subcategory: Cognitive-interview summary overstates prior efficacy
issues.description: Cognitive-interview summary overstates prior efficacy: The synthesis of prior interventions appears internally inconsistent for cognitive interview: the first paragraph says cognitive-interview and Self-Administered Interview findings in the classic misinformation-effect context are quite inconsistent, but the next paragraph’s parenthetical says cognitive interview and reinforced self-affirmation were effective in that same context. If the parenthetical is meant only for reinforced self-affirmation, the current plural wording is misleading.
issues.quote:
The third technique that has been analyzed in the context of memory conformity is cognitive interview (Geiselman, 1984; Ginet et al., 2019), but its effectiveness in eliminating the memory conformity effect has not been demonstrated. In the context of the classic misinformation effect, the results concerning cognitive interview and a related technique, Self-Administered Interview, have been quite inconsistent (Centofanti and Reece, 2006; Gabbert, Hope, Fisher, \& Jamieson, 2012; Holliday and Albon, 2004; Holliday et al., 2012; Paterson, Eijkemans, \& Kemp, 2015; LaPaglia et al., 2014).

In view of the aforementioned studies, it is impossible to unequivocally indicate a technique that is effective in reducing the memory conformity effect: warning produced inconsistent results, while cognitive interview and reinforced self-affirmation were not effective (although they were effective in the context of the classic misinformation effect). Therefore, in the present paper we decided to explore three new ways of reducing the memory conformity effect: (1) extended warning (which in intention is different from the warnings usually applied in existing research as regards its length, detail and breadth); (2) providing detailed knowledge about the fallibility of memory; (3) demonstrating the vulnerability of memory and motivating participants to overcome it.

issues.subcategory: Opening rationale may overrule normative influence too quickly
issues.description: Opening rationale may overrule normative influence too quickly: The assertion that normative impact is “completely ruled out” seems too strong. A private final test removes direct interpersonal pressure at the reporting stage, but the live collaborative recall phase could still create social pressure or public-commitment effects that carry over to later individual reports.
issues.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing. As for false memories, they are possible on the basis of the reasoning and data presented by Wright et al. (2009).

issues.subcategory: Contradiction regarding false memories
issues.description: Contradiction regarding false memories: There seems to be a tension between the statement that the methods are not expected to reduce false-memory-based reports and later mechanistic language suggesting that warnings or education may improve source monitoring and discrepancy detection. The paper should make clear whether the interventions are intended only to change reporting among participants who already remember both sources, or also to reduce source-monitoring failures.
issues.quote: As for false memories, they are possible on the basis of the reasoning and data presented by Wright et al. (2009). In this case we do not expect that our proposed methods will make a memory report less contingent on false information provided by a co-witness.

issues.subcategory: The IMP passage states warning effects too categorically
issues.description: The IMP passage states warning effects too categorically: The preceding sentences use conditional language, but this sentence states the effect of warning as guaranteed. The framework supports a weaker claim: warning and enlightenment should reduce the consistency assumption and may increase reliance on one’s own memory when the original detail can be retrieved and the discrepancy is identified. Recast the sentence in those terms so the theory matches the later caveats about source monitoring and false memories.
issues.quote: However, when the participants are warned about the possible discrepancies between the original and post-event materials and are enlightened i.e., informed about the true purpose of the deception, they no longer assume consistency, search their memory more thoroughly, and when they realize the discrepancies, they rely on their own memory, not on information from the post-event material.

issues.subcategory: Unoperationalized awareness moderation in framework
issues.description: Unoperationalized awareness moderation in framework: The theoretical framework states that the interventions should be more effective among participants who are aware of discrepancies between their own memory and the partner’s misinformation (i.e., correctly monitoring source and content). However, the planned measures and analysis focus on aggregate discussed versus non-discussed accuracy and do not appear to operationalize discrepancy awareness at the item- or participant-level, nor do they specify whether this moderation is confirmatory or exploratory. This creates a gap between the proposed mechanism and what the registered design can evaluate; the study can test overall intervention efficacy but not directly evaluate this narrower mechanism.
issues.quote: From the above reasoning it follows that our methods of reducing the memory conformity effect are directed towards the participants who are aware of the discrepancy between both the original information and the misinformation obtained from the partner. In other words, our methods are expected to be effective in terms of informational influence, as discussed above (Wright et al., 2009). If a person aware of discrepancies was notified of the sources of discrepancies before the individual memory test, there is no reason why they should provide responses in line with the misinformation in that test. On the other hand, if a person who did not discover the discrepancies is notified of possible discrepancies, they do not know what they should avoid. Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.subcategory: Extended warning reveals experimental deception
issues.description: Extended warning reveals experimental deception: The Extended Warning appears to reveal the MORI manipulation by telling participants that the partner saw a different movie version and explaining the deception. If that is part of the actual intervention, this condition tests a highly specific post-warning or enlightenment procedure, so any reduction in conformity may reflect removal of uncertainty about the misinformation source rather than a broader resistance skill. This limits how directly the condition can be compared with, or generalized alongside, interventions that do not reveal the experimental source of the discrepancy.
issues.quote: Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied, should make the participants who are aware of discrepancies discard the consistency assumption and make them rely on their own correct memories.

issues.subcategory: IMP rationale is underspecified in Education about memory
issues.description: IMP rationale is underspecified in Education about memory: The IMP rationale for Education about memory remains somewhat underdeveloped. The paragraph gives relevant support from metamemory and source-monitoring work, and the later caveat acknowledges a possible backfire effect, but it does not fully explain why general education about memory fallibility should weaken the specific consistency assumption in this social setting rather than increasing doubts about the participant's own memory as well as the partner's.
issues.quote: In the present research, we expect that a similar method to the one used by Szpitalak et al (2019) i.e., Education about memory will also be effective in reducing memory conformity. As with the Extended warning, the justification for the hypothesis is grounded in the basic assumptions of the IMP (Blank, 1998). The consistency assumption may cause the participants aware of discrepancies to discard their own correct memories. Drawing their attention to numerous different reasons for giving erroneous reports should prompt them to rethink their own memories, which should support resisting misinformation.

issues.subcategory: Logical tension in the mechanism of resisting misinformation
issues.description: Logical tension in the mechanism of resisting misinformation: The phrase about prompting participants to rethink their own memories creates a local ambiguity in the proposed mechanism. In the context of Seven Sins education, this could be read as increasing self-doubt, which might reinforce rather than weaken the consistency assumption. Although the paper later acknowledges this possible backfire effect, the primary mechanism would be clearer if it distinguished self-doubt from critical source monitoring of both the participant's and the partner's reports.
issues.quote: The consistency assumption may cause the participants aware of discrepancies to discard their own correct memories. Drawing their attention to numerous different reasons for giving erroneous reports should prompt them to rethink their own memories, which should support resisting misinformation.

issues.subcategory: Conflation of psychoeducation with mindfulness
issues.description: Conflation of psychoeducation with mindfulness: The link between the memory-education podcast and mindfulness is not well established here. A lecture about memory fallibility is primarily a metacognitive or psychoeducational manipulation, whereas mindfulness is usually treated as a distinct attentional construct. The cited DRM finding therefore seems only indirectly relevant; it does not show that a memory lecture induces mindfulness or that such a state reduces co-witness conformity. This sentence adds a mechanism the design does not test. Unless the paper explains what form of mindfulness the lecture is expected to induce and how that mechanism differs from the source-monitoring rationale already given, the authors should remove it or make clear that it is only a loose analogy.
issues.quote: A lecture on memory may induce some kind of mindfulness; it should be stressed that mindfulness has been shown to reduce memory errors in the context of the Deese-Roediger-McDermott paradigm (DRM, Calvillo, Flores \& Gonzales, 2018).

issues.subcategory: The education hypothesis has two opposing predicted directions
issues.description: The education hypothesis has two opposing predicted directions: The section first states a directional prediction that education will reduce conformity, then immediately allows the opposite effect through reduced confidence. A caveat is fine, but the registered prediction needs a decision rule. Say which pathway is expected to dominate and how an increase in conformity would be interpreted. For example, the authors could state that improved source monitoring is the primary prediction, while increased conformity would be evidence that the confidence-reduction pathway outweighed the monitoring benefit.
issues.quote:
In sum, it was hypothesized that providing knowledge about memory will contribute to reducing memory conformity.

However, a caveat should be mentioned here: presenting participants with research confirming the fallibility of memory may result in decreased confidence in their own memory, which, in turn, might result in increased suggestibility. Obviously, this was not the case in research by Szpitalak et al. (2019) in the context of the classic misinformation effect, but it is still possible in the proposed experiment. If this is the case, increased memory conformity is possible.

issues.subcategory: The lecture directly targets knowledge, not all metamemory components
issues.description: The lecture directly targets knowledge, not all metamemory components: The described podcast plausibly manipulates declarative knowledge about memory processes. The next sentence extends the expected effect to monitoring, efficacy, and affect, but those are separate constructs and may not move in the same direction. This is especially important because the following caveat says fallibility information may lower confidence, which is close to memory efficacy. Narrow the claim: treat the lecture as a manipulation of knowledge, and label any changes in monitoring, efficacy, or affect as secondary and directionally uncertain unless they will be measured.
issues.quote: In addition, we will introduce participants to the concept of metamemory understood as knowledge about memory and awareness of it (Flavell, 1971). Hultsch, Hertzog, Dixon and Davidson (1988) identified four broad aspects of metamemory: (1) knowledge about memory processes, (2) memory monitoring, (3) sense of memory efficacy, and (4) memory-related affect. The planned lecture on memory functioning refers to the first of these aspects: we expect that it will increase the participants' knowledge about memory processes. We assume that the lecture will also enhance memory monitoring, sense of memory efficacy or even memory-related affect.

issues.subcategory: The McGuire example states the direction of resistance ambiguously
issues.description: The McGuire example states the direction of resistance ambiguously: “Resistance to the truisms” reads as if participants became more resistant to the original beliefs themselves. In the inoculation logic described here, the weak attack is meant to make people more resistant to later attacks on the truism. Revise the last sentence to say “greater resistance to later attacks on these truisms,” which also makes the analogy to protecting an original memory clearer.
issues.quote: McGuire (1964) presented his participants with some cultural truisms (e.g., "you should brush your teeth after every meal") and arguments to weaken them (e.g., "too frequent brushing tends to damage the gums and expose the vulnerable parts of the teeth to decay"). As a result, McGuire (1964) was able to demonstrate greater resistance to the truisms.

issues.subcategory: The Sagarin adaptation omits the diagnostic ability component
issues.description: The Sagarin adaptation omits the diagnostic ability component: The cited Sagarin procedure has two parts: motivation and training in how to diagnose illegitimate influence. The proposed adaptation keeps motivation and adds a DRM demonstration, but it does not teach participants how to distinguish a reliable co-witness statement from a misleading one. The DRM task also demonstrates associative false recall rather than external misinformation from a partner. Either add a diagnostic component to the intervention or narrow the rationale so it does not claim to carry over the full Sagarin mechanism.
issues.quote:
Participants were trained in the 'ability' to differentiate between acceptable and objectionable persuasive messages. This was achieved by teaching participants rules for discriminating between legitimate and illegitimate messages and by informing them that ads may contain illegitimate authorities, which should be regarded as attempts to deceive consumers.

We adapted the ideas from the research described above in the hope that it may be useful in mitigating memory conformity. The demonstration of the fallibility of memory will be done by means of the DRM technique (see detailed description below); the motivational aspect will be achieved by a podcast (i.e., only with sound; no visual material will be included) explaining how harmful a situation is in which one witness reports details that they do not actually remember but which were heard from other witnesses.

issues.subcategory: Intervention timing conflicts across rationale and Procedure
issues.description: Intervention timing conflicts across rationale and Procedure: The intervention timing is internally inconsistent: this passage says the methods will be administered before collaborative recall and before misinformation exposure, whereas Section 2.5 (as well as the Extended Warning rationale) administers them after collaborative recall and before the individual memory test, after the co-witness misinformation has been introduced. Because timing changes the theoretical mechanism being tested (post-warning versus pre-exposure inoculation), the rationale and procedure need to align on whether the study tests pre-exposure inoculation or post-exposure warning/remediation.
issues.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect. In reality, it is most effective to prepare a witness before possible misinformation reaches them.

issues.subcategory: Replication power should not rely on an effect the interventions aim to reduce
issues.description: Replication power should not rely on an effect the interventions aim to reduce: This conclusion is sound only if the replication test is performed in an unprotected condition. The estimate comes from studies without the proposed interventions, but three of the four planned groups are designed to reduce the discussed-versus-non-discussed difference. If the memory conformity effect is tested as an omnibus main effect across all participants, successful interventions would shrink the average effect; in the limiting case where the three intervention arms eliminate conformity, the group-averaged contrast would be about one quarter of the control contrast. Define the replication test as a control-condition test, or provide a separate power justification for the omnibus test under plausible intervention effects.
issues.quote: Under such conditions, the sample size required for $90 \%$ power was 18 . As a much larger sample was assumed, it can be stated that the power to detect the memory conformity effect will be sufficient.

issues.subcategory: Directional tests are not aligned with the stated ANOVA power framework
issues.description: Directional tests are not aligned with the stated ANOVA power framework: The surrounding section uses G*Power’s repeated-measures ANOVA framework, where the interaction test is an F test and is not directional in the usual one-tailed/two-tailed sense. If the planned follow-ups will instead use directional contrasts, the manuscript should specify the contrast model, tail, alpha level, and multiplicity rule, and the power analysis should match that plan. If not, remove the reference to directional significance tests and describe the pairwise tests as non-directional ANOVA contrasts.
issues.quote: For the planned comparisons between two groups, which will be necessary if the general interaction is significant, the required sample sizes are 492,82 , and 34 participants, respectively. Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.

issues.subcategory: Procedures for participants aged 16–17 are missing
issues.description: Procedures for participants aged 16–17 are missing: The lower bound includes minors, and the study involves deception, co-witness discussion, and later debriefing. The participant section should state how age will be verified and what consent or assent procedure will be used for 16- and 17-year-olds under the relevant ethics rules. If minors will not in fact be enrolled, change the age range.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be $16-35$ years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.subcategory: Dyad members must be assigned to opposite MORI versions
issues.description: Dyad members must be assigned to opposite MORI versions: The central manipulation depends on the two members of a dyad seeing different versions of the critical details. The current wording says only that each participant receives glasses blocking one version; read literally, both partners could receive the same orientation, which would remove the discrepant co-witness information. State the dyad-level rule explicitly, for example: one member of each pair receives vertically oriented glasses and the other horizontally oriented glasses, so the partners view opposite versions of the critical details.
issues.quote: Moreover, each participant will receive polarizing glasses that will block one of the two possible versions of the movie. Figure 1 illustrates the MORI technique.

issues.subcategory: Courtroom motivation should be tied to the upcoming test
issues.description: Courtroom motivation should be tied to the upcoming test: The motivational message is framed as advice for a future courtroom setting, but the relevant behavior is the individual memory test they are about to complete. State whether the podcast also gives an immediate task instruction, such as answering from their own memory of the movie and not from information learned from the partner. Without that link, readers cannot tell whether this is general forensic education or a direct instruction for the experimental test.
issues.quote: The participants will also learn that a frequent source of erroneous testimonies is false information from the media or from other witnesses. They will also be instructed that if they ever testify as a witness, they should only use information that they remember.

issues.subcategory: Recognition options introduce a second source of misinformation
issues.description: Recognition options introduce a second source of misinformation: This phase is meant to create co-witness misinformation through the partner’s statements. Displaying five response options adds another post-event source before the partner says anything. If a misinformation-consistent option appears on the slide, a later answer could come from the displayed alternative rather than from memory conformity. A cleaner procedure would show the question without alternatives and let participants state and discuss what they remember; if the recognition format is retained, the analysis needs a plan for separating slide-induced misinformation from partner-induced misinformation.
issues.quote: Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer. If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented. The discussion will be audio recorded.

issues.subcategory: Randomization unit should be the dyad
issues.description: Randomization unit should be the dyad: Randomization needs to be described at the dyad level. The pair has already watched and discussed the event together, and the intervention is delivered within the same session. If partners could be assigned to different arms, the procedure becomes hard to implement and one participant’s materials could contaminate the other’s condition. State that each dyad is randomly assigned to one condition and that both members receive the same intervention or control procedure.
issues.quote: The participants will be randomly divided into four groups: in each of the first three, a different method of minimizing memory conformity will be applied; the fourth group will be the control group.

issues.subcategory: The warning arm is not distinguished from the education arm in the procedure
issues.description: The warning arm is not distinguished from the education arm in the procedure: At the procedural level, the Extended warning and Education conditions sound nearly the same. The theory of the warning condition depends on a co-witness-specific message: participants should learn that information from the discussion may conflict with the version they personally saw. Spell out that element here and explain how the warning podcast differs from the general memory-education podcast. Otherwise the study will not clearly test the intervention described in the rationale.
issues.quote: Participants in the 'Extended warning' group will listen to the podcast about 'memory functioning and its imperfections'; those in in the 'Education about memory' group will listen to the podcast about the functioning and sins of memory.

issues.subcategory: DRM feedback differs for participants who do not recall lures
issues.description: DRM feedback differs for participants who do not recall lures: The condition is described as a personal demonstration of memory distortion, but the script works only for participants who wrote down a critical lure. For participants who did not, “You can see how easily human memory can be distorted” does not follow from their own performance. The same assigned condition would deliver different psychological content. Add a scripted branch for non-lure participants, or define the intervention as a general demonstration using group-level evidence rather than personal feedback.
issues.quote: Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback, described above, which usually results in most of the participants falsely recalling a few of the critical lures. At this moment in this group, the experimenter will give the following information to the participants: "Thank you for completing this memory task. Please take a look at your sheets now. See if you have written down any of the words: doctor, window, sweet, thief. If so, you were fooled. These words are strongly associated with the sets I read, but they were not included in them. You can see how easily human memory can be distorted".

issues.subcategory: Contradictory format of the individual memory test
issues.description: Contradictory format of the individual memory test: The final individual memory-test format is contradictory. Section 2.5 describes a 20-question open-ended test with scoring categories including other answers and total answers, but this passage says the individual memory test will use a two-alternative forced-choice format. The intended format and scoring basis for the primary dependent variables need to be unambiguous.
issues.quote: In existing research using the MORI technique a two-alternative forced-choice questions test was used as the main index of correctness of answers. One of the alternatives matched the correct answer, that is, the item presented to a given participant. The second one, was the alternative consistent with what the partner was presented with. Accordingly, in the scoring system, items in which, during the discussion, the partner of the participant provided an answer consistent with what the partner was familarised with was treated as misleading the participant (e.g., Ito et al. 2019). In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.subcategory: Conflicting misinformation scoring in Section 3
issues.description: Conflicting misinformation scoring in Section 3: The analysis plan appears to use two different rules for coding discussed/misinformation items. It first treats the partner's actual response as determinative, excluding cases where the partner gives the participant's version or says 'don't know,' but then states that all discussed items will be categorized as having contained misinformation. For a registered report, it should be clear whether the main within-subject contrast and the misinformation-consistent response index are based on actual misinformation exposure or on assignment to the discussed-item condition.
issues.quote:
However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen, that is, "white mug" (such a situation can happen, e.g., as a result of the partner's guessing), the situation will not be classified as misleading. Of course, the answer 'don't know' will also not be classified as misleading.

In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version of events.

issues.subcategory: Discussed-item contrast may be confounded in Section 3
issues.description: Discussed-item contrast may be confounded in Section 3: The discussed-versus-non-discussed contrast appears to be confounded unless the item assignment is actually counterbalanced. Section 2.3 says that discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but the Procedure section also says each pair, and apparently all pairs, will discuss the same four critical details. Unless an omitted rotation is intended, discussed status would be confounded with item identity. If the same items are always discussed, the within-subject accuracy difference could reflect item difficulty or salience rather than memory conformity.
issues.quote: Thus, analyzing memory conformity is based on a within-subjects factor. In contrast, the methods of reducing the memory conformity effect constitute a between-subjects factor with four levels (three methods and the control group). The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels (three groups of methods of reducing memory conformity and the control group).

issues.subcategory: Dyad nonindependence in the Section 3 ANOVA
issues.description: Dyad nonindependence in the Section 3 ANOVA: The planned mixed ANOVA does not specify how dyad-level nonindependence will be handled. Because participants interact in pairs and pairs appear to be assigned to intervention condition, a participant-level ANOVA treating all 240 individuals as independent may use an inappropriate error term for the group interaction unless the data are aggregated or modeled with dyad-level clustering.
issues.quote:
Thus, analyzing memory conformity is based on a within-subjects factor. In contrast, the methods of reducing the memory conformity effect constitute a between-subjects factor with four levels (three methods and the control group). The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels (three groups of methods of reducing memory conformity and the control group).

The hypothesis concerning the efficacy of the methods for reducing the memory conformity effect will be verified by means of analyzing the interaction between the repeated measures factor of misinformation and the grouping factor.

issues.subcategory: DRM procedure only administered to one group
issues.description: DRM procedure only administered to one group: The exploratory DRM predictor analysis appears feasible only for the Demonstration and motivation group, because the DRM task is not described as being administered to the other conditions. If the intended analysis is not limited to that group, the procedure and analysis plan are misaligned; if it is limited to that group, the interpretation is condition-specific because DRM performance is part of the intervention rather than an independent baseline measure.
issues.quote:
In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.subcategory: Exclusion rules need dyad-level consequences
issues.description: Exclusion rules need dyad-level consequences: This is too broad for a dyadic misinformation design. If one participant’s glasses, viewing, audio recording, or discussion participation fails, the partner’s misinformation exposure may also be affected. Define which technical problems invalidate the data, whether exclusion is at the participant or dyad level, and which minor issues will be recorded without exclusion. A pre-specified rule will reduce discretion after data collection.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.subcategory: The timeline is no longer written in an actionable way
issues.description: The timeline is no longer written in an actionable way: The timeline should be relative to Stage 1 acceptance, not tied only to 2023. As written, the resubmission deadline is impossible if acceptance occurs after that year; if the study has already been run, the section should say so and give the actual dates. Replace this with intervals for data collection, coding, analysis, and Stage 2 resubmission after acceptance, or update the manuscript to reflect completed work.
issues.quote: The study will be conducted in 2023. If the Stage 1 review is accepted, the resubmission should be completed no later than in 2023.

{"overall": "An overarching goal for a Stage 1 protocol is ensuring the procedure and analysis strategy are unambiguously fixed in advance of data collection. A careful reading of the manuscript reveals a few areas where the planned protocol requires structural clarification before it can support confirmatory inference.

**Intervention timing**

The manuscript currently provides incompatible descriptions of when the interventions will take place. The theoretical layout at the end of Section 1.1.4 states that the techniques will be placed before the collaborative recall phase to "inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect." However, Section 2.5 and Figure 2 place the interventions in Phase 3—after the collaborative recall discussion and just before the individual memory test.

Clarifying this timing is essential for the protocol. A pre-exposure inoculation targets fundamentally different mechanisms than a post-exposure warning or correction. Setting the exact timing will align the registered procedure with its theoretical rationale.

**Primary dependent measure format**

There is an unresolved conflict regarding the format of the primary outcome measure. Section 2.5 states that the individual memory test will contain "20 open-ended questions" and that the data will yield four indices derived from these responses (correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, and overall answers). 

Conversely, Section 3 states that "the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format" and provides a specific scoring paradigm based on a 2AFC structure. Because open-ended and 2AFC tests demand distinct coding rules, handle "other answers" differently, and may require different statistical models, the protocol needs to specify a single, internally consistent format for the primary confirmatory inference.

**Statistical independence and dyadic data**

The proposed statistical plan describes a standard two-factor ANOVA, treating all 240 participants as independent observations. In a MORI design, participants are paired, exposed to each other's answers during collaborative recall, and undergo the intervention together. 

Because participants in the same dyad are non-independent, treating them as independent statistical units inflates degrees of freedom and risks biasing standard errors. The protocol requires an analytical strategy that models dyad-level dependence, whether through mixed-effects models incorporating the dyadic structure or by aggregating outcomes to the session level.

**Item counterbalancing in the recall phase**

Readers might observe a tension regarding the selection of critical items. Section 2.3 states that discussed and non-discussed items will be "fully counterbalanced." However, Section 2.5 says that "each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details," using Eric’s cap color and company logo as examples.

If the same four critical items always serve as the discussed details, the discussed versus non-discussed contrast becomes confounded with item-specific properties such as salience, baseline memorability, or ambiguity. The procedure must explicitly establish how the eight critical items are rotated across the discussed and non-discussed conditions to ensure any observed differences reflect conformity rather than item difficulty.

**Contingencies for the DRM demonstration**

The Demonstration and motivation intervention relies heavily on the participants experiencing a personal instance of memory fallibility, utilizing the DRM false recall paradigm. The text rightly notes that this procedure "usually results in most" participants falsely recalling critical lures.

The scripted feedback in Section 2.5 tells participants, "See if you have written down any of the words... If so, you were fooled." A preregistered protocol must specify a branch for participants who do not falsely recall any of the critical lures.
